a b s t r a c t
The effects of Cr addition on microstructures, mechanical properties and deformation behavior of near-rapidly
solidified low-density Fe-20Mn-9Al-1.2C (wt. %) steel strips were investigated. It was found that Cr addition in-
creased the volume fraction and size of δ-ferrite, and decreased the precipitation of κ-carbides in this low-density
steel strip. The yield strength of the near-rapidly solidified steel strips was decreased significantly, but the ulti-
mate tensile strength and the total elongation didn't obviously change. However, after cold rolling with 20% re-
duction, the yield strength and ultimate tensile strength of Cr-containing steel strips were significantly higher
than that of the Cr-free steel strip. It was attributed to the fact that the decrease of κ-carbides caused by Cr addi-
tion facilitated the formation of high-density slip bands during cold rolling deformation. The ultimate tensile
strength and total elongation of cold-rolled 3Cr (wt. %) steel strip were 1270 MPa and 21%, respectively. A double
(Slip-band and Microband) hardening mechanism was proposed for the strain hardening behavior of the low-
density steel strips, and the number of nanoscale κ-carbides played a crucial role in the strain hardening rate
at the early strain stage.

1. Introduction
Due to increasingly rigorous demands of energy conservation and
emission reduction, the Fe-Mn-Al-C steel with the excellent mechanical
properties and low density has extensive attention in the automotive
field [1–4]. According to the constitution phase, Fe-Mn-Al-C steel is
mainly divided into four categories: fully ferritic steel, fully austenitic
steel, ferrite based duplex steel and austenite based duplex steel [5]. Be-
cause of the effective solid solution and the precipitation hardening of
nano-scale particles, superior mechanical properties are obtained in
the austenite-based duplex steel [6]. This steel consists of the austenite
matrix with the κ-carbide precipitation and a small quantity of ferrite,
also known as TRIPLEX steel [3,6–8]. Due to the high stacking fault en-
ergy (SFE) caused by high Al content, shear band induced plasticity
(SIP), microband induced plasticity (MBIP) and slip band refinement-
induced plasticity (SRIP) are considered as the main deformation mech-
anisms in this steel [6,9–14].

3.1. Microstructures and mechanical properties of steel strips
3.1.1. Microstructures of steel strips
Fig. 1 is X-ray diffraction patterns of the as-cast and annealed low-density Fe-20Mn-
9Al-1.2C-xCr steel strips, which shows that the steel strips mainly consist of austenite
and ferrite. The ferrite should be high temperature δ-ferrite reserved from high tempera-
ture due to the high cooling rate during near-rapid solidification [30]. There is a double-
peak between
and 45.0° in the as-cast steel strips. According to the previous study
[30], one is (110)δ and the other is identified as (220)DO3 with the space group of
Fm3m [35]. The ordered DO3 phase is a body centered cubic crystal with a lattice param-
eter a = 0.565 nm in the ferrite [26], in which Fe or Mn atoms occupy cornered positions,
and Al or Fe/Mn atoms occupy every other centered positions [35]. The area ratio of the
(110)δ peak to (220)DO3 peak gradually decreases with the increase of Cr content.
Thus, the Cr element promotes the transformation from δ-ferrite to the ordered DO3
phase. The double-peak between 43.5° and 45.0° changes into a single-peak when the
steel strips are annealed at 600 °C for 3 h, as shown in Fig. 1 (b). It indicates that almost
all the ferrite transforms into the ordered DO3 phase. Moreover, the intensity of the
single-peak is significantly enhanced with increasing the Cr content in the annealed
steel strips, which indicates that the content of the ordered DO3 phase does increase.
Fig. 2 shows the SEM micrographs of as-cast and annealed Fe-20Mn-9Al-1.2C-xCr
steel strips. It shows that the irregularly shaped δ-ferrite distributes in the γ-austenite ma-
trix, and the Cr addition makes the short rod-shape ferrite change into block ferrite. The
volume fractions of δ-ferrite in the as-cast 0Cr, 3Cr and 6Cr steel strips are
12% and
18%, respectively. And, annealing at 600 °C for 3 h makes the volume fraction of the δ
ferrite in the 0Cr, 3Cr and 6Cr steel strips increase to 6%, 14% and 24%, respectively.

3) Hardening mechanism
J.D. Yoo and K.T. Park [14] proposed that microbands result in con-
tinuous strain hardening of the fully austenitic Fe-28Mn-9Al-0.8C steel
over 80 GPa·%. In contrast to the J.D. Yoo and K.T. Park, E. Welsch et al.
[11] found that the constant high strain hardening rate of the Fe-
30.4Mn-8Al-1.2C steel was attributed to the dynamic slip band refine-
ment. However, it is found there are both slip bands and microbands
in the deforming process of all the studied steel strips. And, formation
of slip bands usually occurs at the early strain stage, and the microbands
appear at the final strain stage. So a double hardening by slip bands and
microbands acts at the different strain stages of this low-density steel.
And at the final strain stage, the strain hardening rate caused by
microbands is usually relatively low.
With respect to the reason for that the strain hardening rate of
annealed 0Cr steel strip shows a clear double hump like feature
shown in Fig. 3 (d). According to the above analysis, the first hump of
the strain hardening rate is related to the slip-band refinement, and
the second is due to the formation of microbands. After the beginning
of plastic deformation, the generation of slip bands leads to the first
hump of the strain hardening rate. As the slip band spacing reaches
the critical value, the strain hardening rate decreases. Under high strain
condition, the generation of microbands results in the second hump of
the strain hardening rate. As strain increases further, the necking occurs
and then specimen fractures by plastic instability. It is emphasized that
the number of nano-scale κ-carbides plays a crucial role in the strain
hardening rate at the early strain stage as discussed above. When the
number of κ-carbides is great, the early strain hardening rate caused
by slip bands is low and similar to that caused by microband hardening
level. This makes the strain hardening rate of the anneal 0Cr steel strip
show a clear double hump like feature as shown in Fig. 3 (d). But
when number of κ-carbides is small as the Cr-containing steel strips,
the early strain hardening rate caused by slip bands is obviously higher
than that caused by microband hardening, which presents a gradually
decrease trend in whole tensile process and the hump like feature be-
comes weaker.

The effect of the addition of Cr on the microstructure, mechanical
properties and deformation behavior of low-density Fe-20Mn-9Al-
1.2C steel strips prepared under near-rapid solidification has been
investigated. According to the obtained results, following conclusions

(1) The constituent phases in the low-density Fe-20Mn-9Al-1.2C-(0,
3, 6)Cr steel strips are mainly austenite and ferrite, and the ferrite
with irregular shape is evenly distributed in the austenite matrix.
The volume fraction and size of ferrite are significantly increased
with the addition of Cr.
(2) There are some nano-scale κ-carbides and ordered DO3 phases in
the austenite and ferrite of the Fe-20Mn-9Al-1.2C steel strips, re-
spectively. With increasing the content of Cr, the volume fraction
of nano-scale κ-carbides decreases.
(3) Due to the decrease of the nano-scale κ-carbides, the Cr addition
decreases the yield strength of the as-cast and annealed steel
strips. However, after cold rolling with 20% reduction, the
strength of Cr-containing steel strips is higher than that of Cr-
free steel strip. The ultimate tensile strength of CR20% 3Cr and
6Cr steel strips reaches 1270 MPa and 1264 MPa, respectively,
and the elongation remains about 21%.
(4) The decrease of the κ-carbide caused by Cr addition could pro-
mote the formation of slip bands at the early strain stage. It re-
sults in the high-density slip bands during deformation and
thereby a higher strain hardening rate of Cr-containing steel
strips.
(5) A double (Slip-band and Microband) hardening mechanism is
proposed in the strain hardening rate of the low-density steel
strips. The hardening of slip bands and microbands acts at the
early and final stages of the deformation process, respectively.

(1) The constituent phases in the low-density Fe-20Mn-9Al-1.2C-(0,
3, 6)Cr steel strips are mainly austenite and ferrite, and the ferrite
with irregular shape is evenly distributed in the austenite matrix.
The volume fraction and size of ferrite are significantly increased
with the addition of Cr.
(2) There are some nano-scale κ-carbides and ordered DO3 phases in
the austenite and ferrite of the Fe-20Mn-9Al-1.2C steel strips, re-
spectively. With increasing the content of Cr, the volume fraction
of nano-scale κ-carbides decreases.
(3) Due to the decrease of the nano-scale κ-carbides, the Cr addition
decreases the yield strength of the as-cast and annealed steel
strips. However, after cold rolling with 20% reduction, the
strength of Cr-containing steel strips is higher than that of Cr-
free steel strip. The ultimate tensile strength of CR20% 3Cr and
6Cr steel strips reaches 1270 MPa and 1264 MPa, respectively,
and the elongation remains about 21%.
(4) The decrease of the κ-carbide caused by Cr addition could pro-
mote the formation of slip bands at the early strain stage. It re-
sults in the high-density slip bands during deformation and
thereby a higher strain hardening rate of Cr-containing steel
strips.
(5) A double (Slip-band and Microband) hardening mechanism is
proposed in the strain hardening rate of the low-density steel
strips. The hardening of slip bands and microbands acts at the
early and final stages of the deformation process, respectively.
